title: SMS Permissions Combination
description: App has both SMS read and send permissions, which could be used for premium SMS fraud
analystDescription: The application declares both SMS read and send permissions. This combination is commonly seen in malware that sends premium-rate SMS messages or exfiltrates SMS content.
limitations: Permission declaration does not guarantee usage
recommendations: Review if SMS functionality is necessary
Verify SMS recipients are not premium numbers

title: Exported Content Provider
description: App has an exported content provider, which could expose sensitive data
analystDescription: The application declares an exported content provider. Exported providers can be accessed by other applications, potentially exposing sensitive data or allowing unauthorized data modification.
limitations: Provider may have permission checks in code
recommendations: Verify provider has proper permission checks
Consider if provider needs to be exported

title: Exported Component Without Permission
description: App has an exported component without permission protection
analystDescription: The application has exported components that do not require permissions to access. This allows any application on the device to interact with these components.
limitations: Component may validate caller identity in code
recommendations: Add permission protection to exported components
Verify component validates caller identity

title: Application is Debuggable
description: App is marked as debuggable, which should not be present in production
analystDescription: The android:debuggable flag is set to true in the manifest. This allows debuggers to attach to the process and should never be present in production builds as it poses a significant security risk.
recommendations: Remove debuggable flag for production releases
Verify build configuration

title: Cleartext Traffic Permitted
analystDescription: The android:usesCleartextTraffic flag is set to true, allowing unencrypted HTTP traffic. This can expose user data to network eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.
limitations: May be intentional for development or specific use cases
recommendations: Use HTTPS for all network communication
Implement network security configuration

title: Outdated Target SDK
description: App targets an outdated SDK version, missing modern security protections
analystDescription: The application targets an SDK version below 30, which means it may not benefit from modern Android security protections and behavioral changes.
limitations: App may still be secure with proper implementation
recommendations: Update target SDK to latest version
Review behavioral changes in newer Android versions

title: Background Location Access
description: App has location permissions that could be used for background tracking
analystDescription: The application has fine or coarse location permissions. While location access may be legitimate, it could also be used for user tracking without explicit consent.
recommendations: Verify location access is user-initiated
Check if background location is necessary

title: Dynamic Code Loading with Storage Access
description: App loads code dynamically and has storage access permissions, a combination sometimes used to execute downloaded payloads
analystDescription: The application uses DexClassLoader or PathClassLoader to load code dynamically and also declares storage read/write permissions. While each can be legitimate, together they can enable downloading and executing external payloads.
limitations: Storage access may be used for legitimate file operations
Dynamic loading may be used by legitimate plugin architectures
recommendations: Verify dynamic loading is necessary and constrained
Review downloaded content sources

title: Shell Command Execution Detected
description: App contains code that can execute shell commands
analystDescription: The application references Runtime.exec or ProcessBuilder with reconstructible command strings. This is a strong indicator of capability to execute arbitrary shell commands, which is frequently abused by malware.
limitations: Command strings may be benign (e.g., reading device info)
Static analysis cannot prove commands execute
recommendations: Inspect reconstructed command strings
Avoid executing shell commands from untrusted inputs

title: Reflection Combined with Network Capability
description: App uses reflection and has network permissions, a combination sometimes used to conceal malicious behavior
analystDescription: The application declares the INTERNET permission and uses reflection (Class.forName or Method.invoke). Reflection can be used to hide API calls from static analysis, and combined with network access it may fetch or execute remote logic.
limitations: Reflection is common in legitimate libraries and frameworks
Network access alone is normal for most apps
recommendations: Review reflected classes and methods
Verify network destinations are trustworthy

title: SMS Permissions with Code References
description: App declares SMS permissions and references SMS-related APIs in code
analystDescription: The application declares SMS permissions and its code references SMS APIs. This increases confidence that the declared permissions are actively used, which is relevant for premium SMS fraud and SMS exfiltration analysis.
limitations: SMS functionality may be legitimate (e.g., two-factor authentication)
recommendations: Verify SMS recipients and message content
Check if SMS permission is necessary

title: Accessibility Service with Overlay Permission
description: App declares accessibility service and overlay permission, a combination often used for screen interaction attacks
analystDescription: The application declares an accessibility service and the SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW permission. Together these capabilities can interact with screen content and draw over other applications, which is a common pattern in remote-control and credential-theft malware.
limitations: Accessibility services are legitimate for assistive technology
Overlay permission may be used for legitimate floating UI
recommendations: Verify publisher and purpose before enabling accessibility
Review overlay usage
